statement: The function returns a result r and r = max { safe(P) : P is a path from (0,0) to (n-1,n-1) }. Here d(i,j) = min { |i-a| + |j-b| : 0 <= a,b < n and grid[a][b] = 1 } for every cell (i,j) in the grid. A path P is a finite sequence of cells p_0,...,p_k with k >= 0, p_0 = (0,0), p_k = (n-1,n-1), every p_t in the grid, no cell repeated in the sequence, and p_{t+1} adjacent to p_t (that is, |r_{t+1}-r_t| + |c_{t+1}-c_t| = 1) for every 0 <= t < k. safe(P) = min { d(p_t) : 0 <= t <= k }. Equivalently, r is the largest integer s >= 0 for which there exists a path from (0,0) to (n-1,n-1) such that d(q) >= s for every cell q on the path.
preconditions: Assume n = len(grid), 1 <= n <= 400, len(grid[i]) = n for every i with 0 <= i < n, grid[i][j] is 0 or 1 for every 0 <= i,j < n, and there exists at least one pair (a,b) with 0 <= a,b < n and grid[a][b] = 1.

statement: With d(i,j) = min { |i-a| + |j-b| : 0 <= a,b < n and grid[a][b] = 1 } and paths defined as finite sequences p_0,...,p_k with p_0=(0,0), p_k=(n-1,n-1), all cells in the grid, no repeated cell, consecutive cells adjacent by Manhattan distance 1, and safe(P) = min { d(p_t) : 0 <= t <= k }, the function returns a result r and there exists a path P from (0,0) to (n-1,n-1) such that safe(P) = r.

statement: Let d(i,j) = min { |i-a| + |j-b| : 0 <= a,b < n and grid[a][b] = 1 }. The function returns a result r and for every integer s, s <= r if and only if there exists a path P from (0,0) to (n-1,n-1) (a finite sequence of cells with p_0=(0,0), p_k=(n-1,n-1), all cells in the grid, no repeated cell, and consecutive cells adjacent by Manhattan distance 1) such that d(q) >= s for every cell q occurring in P.
preconditions: Assume n = len(grid), 1 <= n <= 400, len(grid[i]) = n for every i with 0 <= i < n, grid[i][j] is 0 or 1 for every 0 <= i,j < n, and there exists at least one pair (a,b) with 0 <= a,b < n and grid[a][b] = 1.

statement: Let r be the result returned by maximum_safeness_factor(grid) and let r2 be the result returned by maximum_safeness_factor(grid2). Then both calls return results and r2 <= r.
preconditions: Assume n = len(grid) = len(grid2), 1 <= n <= 400, len(grid[i]) = len(grid2[i]) = n for every 0 <= i < n, all entries of grid and grid2 are 0 or 1, grid contains at least one 1, and grid[i][j] <= grid2[i][j] for every 0 <= i,j < n.
